title: Anyone with a member's friend link can put a stranger's number in as an enquiry, and the gym then contacts someone who never asked
what: The bring-a-friend form takes any name and any Indian mobile number and sends it to the gym as an enquiry. Nothing proves the number belongs to the person who typed it, unlike the Become a member form, which needs a WhatsApp check. One person changing network address can fill a gym's 30 friend enquiries a day with strangers' numbers, so the gym calls or messages people who never agreed, and real friends are refused for the day.
expected: A friend enquiry is only kept once the friend has shown the number is theirs (as the join form does), or the gym is told the number is not checked before it contacts them.
who: gym owners and the people whose numbers are typed
how_often: whenever someone misuses a friend link
fix_line: Ask the friend to confirm the number by WhatsApp before the enquiry reaches the gym, or mark it unchecked

title: An outsider can fill the day's crash reports and plant made-up crash notes that our coding sessions later read
what: The crash address accepts reports from anyone, 30 per network address and 2000 in all per day. A person with about 70 addresses fills the day, so real crashes from the apps are refused until the next day. Each made-up report also becomes one of the 5 new crash issues opened each day, with the sender's own text in it, and that text is later read by the AI coding sessions that work through crash issues, so it can try to steer them.
expected: Only the real apps can send crash reports, one flood cannot push out real ones, and crash text in an issue is clearly marked as outside text that must never be followed.
fix_line: Sign crash reports from the apps, cap per kind not only in total, and mark issue text as untrusted
